title: OOP: a BankAccount class
prompt:
Complete the BankAccount class in the starter code:

  - __construct(string $owner, float $balance = 0.0) stores both values in private properties
  - deposit(float $amount): void  — adds to the balance
  - withdraw(float $amount): void — subtracts from the balance

Rules (use exceptions, not return codes):
  - deposit/withdraw must throw new InvalidArgumentException('Amount must be positive') when $amount <= 0
  - withdraw must throw new InvalidArgumentException('Insufficient funds') when the balance is too low

The tests call the runAccount() wrapper at the bottom of the starter code. It is already complete — leave it as is.

hints: Declare properties at the top of the class: private string $owner; private float $balance; and assign them in the constructor with $this->owner = $owner;.
Both deposit and withdraw start with: if ($amount <= 0) { throw new InvalidArgumentException('Amount must be positive'); }
In withdraw, after the amount check: if ($amount > $this->balance) { throw new InvalidArgumentException('Insufficient funds'); }. The exact messages matter — the wrapper collects them.
solution:
<?php
class BankAccount
{
    private string $owner;
    private float $balance;

    public function __construct(string $owner, float $balance = 0.0)
    {
        $this->owner = $owner;
        $this->balance = $balance;
    }

    public function deposit(float $amount): void
    {
        $this->assertPositive($amount);
        $this->balance += $amount;
    }

    public function withdraw(float $amount): void
    {
        $this->assertPositive($amount);
        if ($amount > $this->balance) {
            throw new InvalidArgumentException('Insufficient funds');
        }
        $this->balance -= $amount;
    }

    public function getOwner(): string
    {
        return $this->owner;
    }

    public function getBalance(): float
    {
        return $this->balance;
    }

    private function assertPositive(float $amount): void
    {
        if ($amount <= 0) {
            throw new InvalidArgumentException('Amount must be positive');
        }
    }
}

function runAccount(string $owner, array $operations): array
{
    $account = new BankAccount($owner);
    $errors = [];

    foreach ($operations as [$action, $amount]) {
        try {
            match ($action) {
                'deposit'  => $account->deposit($amount),
                'withdraw' => $account->withdraw($amount),
            };
        } catch (InvalidArgumentException $e) {
            $errors[] = $e->getMessage();
        }
    }

    return [
        'owner'   => $account->getOwner(),
        'balance' => $account->getBalance(),
        'errors'  => $errors,
    ];
}
